The bug is in the String-based parsing methods of `ClassUtils`, not the `Class<?>` overloads.

Diagnosis:
- `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?>)` simply delegates to `getShortClassName(cls.getName())`.
- `ClassUtils.getPackageName(Class<?>)` simply delegates to `getPackageName(cls.getName())`.

For `String[].class`, `cls.getName()` is the JVM descriptor:
- `"[Ljava.lang.String;"`

The broken behavior matches the current code exactly:

1. `getShortClassName(String)`
- It has comments saying it should “Handle array encoding” / “Strip Object type encoding”
- But there is no implementation there
- It just finds the last `.` and returns the suffix
- For `"[Ljava.lang.String;"`, that suffix is `"String;"`, which explains the failure:
  - expected: `String[]`
  - actual: `String;`

2. `getPackageName(String)`
- It also has comments saying it should strip array/object encoding
- But again, no implementation exists
- It returns everything before the last `.`
- For `"[Ljava.lang.String;"`, that becomes `"[Ljava.lang"`, which explains the failure:
  - expected: `java.lang`
  - actual: `[Ljava.lang`

So the root cause is: array class names in JVM descriptor form are not decoded before extracting short class name or package name.

Best fix locations:
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getPackageName(java.lang.String)

m20.content:
The bug is in the String-based parsing methods of `ClassUtils`, not the `Class<?>` overloads.

Diagnosis:
- `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?>)` simply delegates to `getShortClassName(cls.getName())`.
- `ClassUtils.getPackageName(Class<?>)` simply delegates to `getPackageName(cls.getName())`.

For `String[].class`, `cls.getName()` is the JVM descriptor:
- `"[Ljava.lang.String;"`

The broken behavior matches the current code exactly:

1. `getShortClassName(String)`
- It has comments saying it should “Handle array encoding” / “Strip Object type encoding”
- But there is no implementation there
- It just finds the last `.` and returns the suffix
- For `"[Ljava.lang.String;"`, that suffix is `"String;"`, which explains the failure:
  - expected: `String[]`
  - actual: `String;`

2. `getPackageName(String)`
- It also has comments saying it should strip array/object encoding
- But again, no implementation exists
- It returns everything before the last `.`
- For `"[Ljava.lang.String;"`, that becomes `"[Ljava.lang"`, which explains the failure:
  - expected: `java.lang`
  - actual: `[Ljava.lang`

So the root cause is: array class names in JVM descriptor form are not decoded before extracting short class name or package name.

Best fix locations:
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getPackageName(java.lang.String)
